articles.title: Experience: I’m allergic to the cold
articles.summary: My condition is severe, so I have to a keep close watch on my body temperature and can’t eat chilled foods. In 2012, when I was 37, I started noticing that my fingers would get swollen and red whenever I held an iced drink. I thought it was strange, but I didn’t know what was going on.
body: For a while, that’s all I experienced. I thought it was weird but not dangerous. I was busy with my three children, so didn’t worry.
But then other areas of my body started to react. Once, I was eating ice-cream when the inside of my cheeks started swelling and my tongue felt weird. It was scary.

In the spring of 2014, I went to the doctor. They referred me to an allergist for a test – they put an ice cube inside a metal container and stick it on your arm, cover it up and leave it for 10 minutes. When they take it off, they watch to see what happens as your body warms up. That is generally when the hives and swelling start.

The allergist confirmed I had cold urticaria, a rare condition that means you’re allergic to the cold, and that it was a severe allergy, meaning I could have an anaphylactic reaction. The doctor prescribed me some EpiPens and said I could take antihistamines, but that they didn’t always work.

articles.title: A century after the weekend was invented, it has disappeared. Let’s reclaim leisure | Richard Morgan
articles.summary: Henry Ford’s 1926 policy held for decades before eroding into a 24/7 mindset. Here’s what we can do about it. It was a Saturday. In fact, the Saturday. Almost exactly a century ago, on 25 September 1926, Henry Ford instituted a policy of weekends for his workforce.
body: It caught on, buoyed by portraits of leisure gracing the covers of the Saturday Evening Post, drawn by an idealistic young artist from New York named Norman Rockwell. In 1929, Walt Disney leveraged Saturday matinees of his animated films to launch The Mickey Mouse Club. On Saturday 25 June 1938, President Franklin Roosevelt passed the Fair Labor Standards Act, formalizing the weekend as federal policy.

Beyond workplace respite, the weekend began to form its own identity. In 1944, Frank Sinatra popularized Saturday as “the loneliest night of the week, because that’s the night my sweetie and I used to dance cheek-to-cheek”. And the 1948 lyrics to Tennessee Saturday Night blared: “Civilized people live there alright, but they all go native on a Saturday night.”

The postwar boom of suburban pleasures transformed weekends into an anchor of indulgence. Sábado Gigante in 1962. Saturday morning cartoons in 1963. The launch of TGIFriday’s as a singles bar in 1965. Super Bowl Sunday in 1967. And a banner year, 1969, saw the moon landing on a Sunday followed by a weekend of Woodstock.
points: Henry Ford’s 1926 policy held for decades before eroding into a 24/7 mindset.

articles.summary: Shop the just-dropped Baisi Guadagnino for Zara collection—a collaboration between architect and production designer Stefano Baisi and filmmaker Luca Guadagnino.
body: From fall’s biggest trends to cold-weather wardrobe staples, Zara’s new arrivals section offers plenty of reasons to browse right now. But the most intriguing arrival this week is Baisi Guadagnino for Zara. Dubbed “Atlas of Desire,” the collaboration comes from architect and production designer Stefano Baisi and Challengers filmmaker Luca Guadagnino, longtime creative partners whose lush cinematic sensibility translates into equally expressive clothes.

Painterly prints mingle with pops of rich colors and pastels (notably the trendy turquoise ), while reversible outerwear works double duty. Accessories exude visual personality, from sculptural brooches and printed scarves to tactile clutches, designed as finishing-touch “objects” rather than dressing afterthoughts.

articles.title: Is Your Beauty Brand Actually Ready for Retail?
articles.summary: Securing a shelf at Sephora or Ulta can take a budding beauty brand to new heights. But succeeding once you’re in the door requires strong operations behind the scenes.
body: For beauty founders, launching your brand in retail stores carries symbolic weight. A major stockist logo can signal credibility, unlock visibility, and turn a promising challenger into a serious player. But in today’s market, securing distribution is no longer the same as being commercially ready for it.

The route to scale is increasingly fragmented and demanding, with brands navigating direct-to-consumer, specialist retail, department stores, Amazon, TikTok Shop, affiliates, and creator-led commerce at once. Retail is not just a badge of arrival, it’s an operating model, and a demanding one. Inventory has to be available at the right time, margins have to absorb retailer terms, teams have to support education and marketing, and sell-through has to be sustained beyond the launch. Getting picked up is one challenge, staying on the shelf is another.
points: Securing a shelf at Sephora or Ulta can take a budding beauty brand to new heights.
But succeeding once you’re in the door requires strong operations behind the scenes.

articles.title: What Is a Neuro-Wellness Spa Retreat—and Why Are Travelers Flocking to Them?
articles.summary: A travel writer with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease grapples with the wellness trend of neurological optimization that aims to make the mind sharper—and perhaps less disease-prone.
body: I arrived at Palace Merano, the storied wellness getaway in South Tyrol near the Italian Dolomites, utterly famished. After an early-morning flight to Venice, followed by a four-hour drive, I want to collapse in bed almost as much as I want a snack. Once I get to my room I’m dreaming of raiding the mini bar or devouring a complimentary fruit basket when I look around to see—nothing. No nectarines or oranges or grapes, no tray of sweets; I thrust open the doors of the armoire, but all I see is a large bottle of mineral water and a selection of caffeine-free herbal teas. There’s even no coffee machine, let alone coffee.
points: A travel writer with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease grapples with the wellness trend of neurological optimization that aims to make the mind sharper—and perhaps less disease-prone.
